::: {#rem-fallacies}
#### Two arguments that are not rules of inference

Argument 2 of @exr-valid-arguments,
$\dfrac{P \Rightarrow Q, \quad Q}{P}$,
is called affirming the consequent,
since it concludes $P$ from the consequent $Q$ of $P \Rightarrow Q$ (@rem-implies-terms).
It is not a rule of inference (@def-rule-of-inference):
$P$ false and $Q$ true make its premises true and its conclusion false.

Denying the antecedent,
$\dfrac{P \Rightarrow Q, \quad \neg P}{\neg Q}$,
fails for the same values of $P$ and $Q$.
Both read like modus ponens or modus tollens (@thm-inference-rules),
which is why they are common mistakes.

:::
